entry.title: Unique Identifiers in Android and iOS: ANDROID_ID, UUID, and Other Strategies
entry.summary:
In mobile app development, it is common to need a unique identifier that consistently recognizes each device — whether for analytics, personalization, licensing, or usage tracking. However, obtaining and managing that identifier can be tricky due to privacy policies, platform-specific restrictions, and various events that can cause the identifier to change. The value of ANDROID_ID is defined based on three factors: the app’s signing key, the user, and the device. This means: Each combination of app, user, and device has a unique ANDROID_ID.
If two apps have different signing keys, even on the same device and same user, they will not share the same ANDROID_ID.
